free_tier.stated: 'New workspaces get $30 of free credit, once per person ... and the tour starts a box on it with no card. It does not refill.' While on the credit alone: sizes Nano to Small only, one box at a time, no process at full CPU for more than 30 minutes.
free_tier.notes: Smallest grant, but the only one whose meters let a single credit run a box for multiple months.

per_object_cap.stated: On the free credit 'Nano, Micro, Extra Small, or Small only'; Medium and larger answer `409 tier_unavailable`. A Nano is 2 vCPU / 2 GB / 40 GB at USD 0.014 an hour awake.
per_object_cap.notes: A Small is 4 vCPU / 16 GB / 300 GB at USD 0.137 an hour, which burns the whole USD 30 in nine days.

retention.stated: Asleep, a box costs only its disk at USD 0.0001 per GB-hour; a Small asleep for a month is about USD 22. Credit rolls over up to two months of the plan.

egress.terms: No egress charge or allowance is stated on the billing page.

limits.value: USD 30 one-time free credit, once per person
one box at a time on the credit
no process at full CPU for more than 30 minutes on the credit

limits_note: The 30-minute full-CPU rule can pause the workspace and answer 409 workspace_held on the next create or wake; it is a use cap that no other provider here imposes.

identity_cost.detail: 'the tour starts a box on it with no card' and the credit is once per person by email or by Google or GitHub account. No card, no phone, no ID at signup; paid plans use Stripe Checkout, cards only.

reliability_note: On the credit a box auto-pauses itself after 2 hours idle unless the window is changed or switched off per box; it never pauses in its first 24 hours.
confidence_note: Every number is from the billing page read today. Not observed: whether the 30-minute CPU rule is enforced by cgroup throttling or by pausing, which decides whether a long build is slowed or killed.

evidence.proved: 'Nano (nano) 2 vCPU / 2 GB, 40 GB, $0.014 an hour awake, $0.004 an hour asleep, $10 a month to run 24/7' with 'Pausing keeps the money' and 'While the workspace runs on the free credit alone: One box at a time' and 'Credit rolls over up to two months', quoted

quoted: 'New workspaces get $30 of free credit, once per person, as the owner walks through onboarding or first signs in with `prized login` through the browser; it spends like paid credit, and the tour starts a box on it with no card.'; 'Awake around the clock, the credit lasts about three months on a Nano, five weeks on a Micro, nine days on a Small'; 'No process at full CPU for more than 30 minutes'.
quoted box table: 'Nano (`nano`) | 2 vCPU / 2 GB | 40 GB | $0.014 an hour | $0.004 an hour | $10 a month'; 'Small (`flow`) | 4 vCPU / 16 GB | 300 GB | $0.137 an hour'.

notes: USD 30 / USD 0.014 = 2,143 hours, which is 89 days of a 2 vCPU / 2 GB box with no card. The page's own claim of 'about three months on a Nano' matches. This is the longest no-card calendar coverage and it is a real VM, not a sandbox, but a 2 vCPU / 2 GB box is also the smallest shape any row here offers for a full month.

extras.billing_model: per-second while awake, per GB-hour while asleep

session_cap.note: 2-hour idle auto-pause by default on the credit; can be changed per box or switched off

extras.credit_expiry: does not refill; rollover on a paid plan is two months

binding_note: The 30-minute full-CPU rule is what fails first for any real build; the credit itself is generous at the Nano size.
